content: 1. When ramelteon is co-administered with ciprofloxacin, the patient should be closely monitored for signs of toxicity due to potential interactions affecting the metabolism of ramelteon. 2. Ciprofloxacin and ranolazine both have the potential to prolong the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored for any cardiac effects. Although ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval, caution is necessary when combined with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 3. Ciprofloxacin can enhance the effects of repaglinide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Careful monitoring of blood glucose levels is recommended, as both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised when rilpivirine is co-administered with drugs that carry a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 5. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of riluzole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Patients should be monitored for potential adverse effects. 6. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of ropinirole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially decreasing its metabolism. Patients should be monitored for increased effects or toxicity of ropinirole. 7. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of ropivacaine by decreasing its metabolism. Patients should be monitored for signs of increased ropivacaine toxicity. 8. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of rosiglitazone through pharmacodynamic synergy. Blood glucose levels should be carefully monitored due to the risk of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 9. Sarecycline increases the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates, and dosage adjustments may be required. 10. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of saxagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Blood glucose levels should be carefully monitored due to the risk of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 11. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Sertraline and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Sevelamer reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer oral quinolones at least 1 hour before or 3 hours after sevelamer to minimize interaction. 14. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of sitagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Blood glucose levels should be carefully monitored due to the risk of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 15. Sodium bicarbonate reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alkaline urine caused by urinary alkalinizing agents like sodium bicarbonate can decrease ciprofloxacin solubility, increasing the risk of crystalluria and nephrotoxicity. Patients should be monitored for these adverse effects. 16. Sodium citrate/citric acid reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alkaline urine caused by urinary alkalinizing agents like sodium citrate can decrease ciprofloxacin solubility, increasing the risk of crystalluria and nephrotoxicity. Patients should be monitored for these adverse effects. 17. Ciprofloxacin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Additionally, these agents reduce ciprofloxacin levels through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. To avoid magnesium chelation, ciprofloxacin should be taken at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after administration of these agents. 18. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 19. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer fluoroquinolones at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 20. Solifenacin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Sorafenib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Ciprofloxacin and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Although ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval, caution is necessary when combined with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 23. Stiripentol increases ciprofloxacin levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur during concomitant administration. 24. Sucralfate reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To avoid chelation, ciprofloxacin should be taken 2 hours before or 6 hours after sucralfate administration. 25. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids, such as triamcinolone acetonide, may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Multivalent cation-containing products may reduce quinolone bioavailability; administer quinolones at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. 27. Triptorelin increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Tucatinib increases ciprofloxacin levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 29. Vadadustat increases ciprofloxacin levels or effects by affecting OAT3 substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects and reduce substrate doses as per product labeling. 30. Valbenazine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of vildagliptin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Blood glucose levels should be carefully monitored due to the risk of hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. 32. Voclosporin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Vorinostat and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Ciprofloxacin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Zinc reduces ciprofloxacin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Ciprofloxacin should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after zinc salts to avoid interaction. 36. Ciprofloxacin and ziprasidone both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Although ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval, caution is necessary when combined with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 37. Ciprofloxacin increases zolpidem levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Ciprofloxacin increases acebutolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 39. Ciprofloxacin increases alprazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 40. Ciprofloxacin decreases balsalazide levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Ciprofloxacin increases carvedilol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 42. Ciprofloxacin increases chlordiazepoxide levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 43. Ciprofloxacin increases clonazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 44. Ciprofloxacin increases clorazepate levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 45. Ciprofloxacin increases diazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 46. Ciprofloxacin increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Ciprofloxacin increases esmolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 48. Ciprofloxacin increases estazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 49. Fennel reduces ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Fennel should be taken at least 1 hour after ciprofloxacin administration. 50. Ciprofloxacin increases flurazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 51. Ciprofloxacin and foscarnet may increase the risk of seizures. The mechanism is unknown, and the clinical significance is unclear. 52. Ciprofloxacin increases frovatriptan levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 53. Ciprofloxacin increases green tea levels by decreasing its elimination. Some quinolones can inhibit the hepatic clearance of caffeine. Caution is advised. 54. Ciprofloxacin and isotretinoin both increase the risk of phototoxicity. Caution is advised with concomitant use. 55. Ciprofloxacin increases metoprolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 56. Ciprofloxacin increases midazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 57. Ciprofloxacin increases nadolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 58. Ciprofloxacin increases nebivolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 59. Ciprofloxacin increases penbutolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 60. Ciprofloxacin increases pindolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 61. Ciprofloxacin increases propranolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 62. Ciprofloxacin decreases pyridoxine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Ciprofloxacin increases quazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 64. Quercetin reduces ciprofloxacin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Ciprofloxacin increases ruxolitinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 66. Ciprofloxacin increases ruxolitinib topical levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 67. Ciprofloxacin increases temazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 68. Ciprofloxacin decreases thiamine levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown.
